title: Ohm's law: a battery and a resistor
description: A 5 V source drives 1 kΩ. Ohm's law says the current is I = V / R = 5 mA.

title: Voltage divider
description: Two resistors in series split 12 V. The middle node sits at 12 · R2 / (R1 + R2) = 4 V.
netlist:
* Voltage divider
V1 in 0 12
R1 in out 8k
R2 out 0 4k
.end

title: Voltage source with a series and a shunt resistor
description: 12 V across 3 Ω and 6 Ω in series. The voltage source adds its current as an extra unknown in the MNA system.
netlist:
* Voltage source and two resistors
V1 1 0 12.0
R1 1 2 3.0
R2 2 0 6.0
.end

title: Current source into a resistor network
description: A 3 A current source feeds four resistors. A good first system to write by hand: three nodes, three KCL equations.
netlist:
* Current source network
I1 0 1 3.0
R1 1 2 5.0
R2 2 0 10.0
R3 2 3 5.0
R4 3 0 10.0
.end

title: Two parallel branches
description: A 4 A source splits between two resistor branches. The branch with less resistance takes more current.
netlist:
* Parallel branches
I1 0 1 4.0
R1 1 2 4.0
R2 2 0 8.0
R3 1 3 2.0
R4 3 0 6.0
.end

title: Resistor ladder
description: A 10 A source drives a three-rung ladder of 6 Ω and 12 Ω resistors. Each rung halves the voltage.

title: Wheatstone bridge
description: Two dividers side by side with a 50 Ω resistor across the middle. When the bridge is unbalanced, current flows through it.

title: RC charging
description: A 5 V step charges 1 µF through 1 kΩ. The time constant τ = RC = 1 ms: after 1 ms the capacitor reaches 63 % of 5 V.
netlist:
* RC charging, tau = 1 ms
V1 1 0 PULSE(0 5 0 1n 1n)
R1 1 2 1k
C1 2 0 1u
.tran 10u 5m
.end

title: Square wave into an RC filter
description: A 1 kHz square wave through 1 kΩ and 100 nF. The capacitor rounds off every edge.
netlist:
* Square wave into RC
V1 1 0 PULSE(0 5 0 1n 1n 500u 1m)
R1 1 2 1k
C1 2 0 100n
.tran 5u 3m
.end

title: Series RLC ringing
description: A 1 V step into 10 Ω, 1 mH and 1 µF. The capacitor voltage overshoots and rings at about 5 kHz before settling.
netlist:
* Series RLC step response
V1 1 0 PULSE(0 1 0 1n 1n)
R1 1 2 10
L1 2 3 1m
C1 3 0 1u
.tran 2u 1m
.end

title: RC low-pass filter (Bode plot)
description: 1 kΩ and 159 nF give a cutoff of about 1 kHz. Above it the output falls by 20 dB per decade.
netlist:
* RC low-pass, fc ~ 1 kHz
V1 in 0 DC 0 AC 1
R1 in out 1k
C1 out 0 159n
.ac dec 20 10 100k
.end

title: LED with a current-limiting resistor
description: 5 V drives an LED through 330 Ω. The LED only conducts above about 1.8 V, and the resistor sets the current.
netlist:
* LED and resistor
V1 1 0 5
R1 1 2 330
D1 2 0 LED
.model LED D(IS=1e-19 N=1.8)
.end

title: Diode I-V curve
description: Sweeps the voltage across a silicon diode from 0 to 0.8 V. Almost no current flows until about 0.6 V, then it shoots up.
netlist:
* Diode characteristic
V1 a 0 0
D1 a 0 DSI
.model DSI D(IS=1e-14 N=1)
.dc V1 0 0.8 0.005
.end

title: Half-wave rectifier
description: A 5 V sine wave through a diode into 1 kΩ. Only the positive half-cycles get through.
netlist:
* Half-wave rectifier
V1 in 0 SIN(0 5 1k)
D1 in out DR
R1 out 0 1k
.model DR D(IS=1e-14)
.tran 10u 3m
.end

title: BJT common-emitter amplifier
description: A transistor biased by a 47k/10k divider amplifies a small AC input. The AC sweep shows the gain and where it rolls off.
netlist:
* Common-emitter amplifier
VCC vcc 0 12
VS in 0 DC 0 AC 1m
CIN in b 10u
R1 vcc b 47k
R2 b 0 10k
RC vcc c 2.2k
RE e 0 1k
CE e 0 100u
Q1 c b e QN
.model QN NPN(IS=1e-15 BF=150)
.ac dec 20 1 1meg
.end

title: CMOS inverter
description: A PMOS pulls the output up and an NMOS pulls it down. Sweeping the input from 0 to 5 V shows the logic switch near 2.5 V.
netlist:
* CMOS inverter
VDD vdd 0 5
VIN in 0 0
MP out in vdd PM W=20u L=1u
MN out in 0 NM W=10u L=1u
.model NM NMOS(VTO=0.8 KP=100u LAMBDA=0.01)
.model PM PMOS(VTO=-0.8 KP=50u LAMBDA=0.01)
.dc VIN 0 5 0.02
.end
